description: Canonical mapping from canonical operation_id (artifacts/registry/operation-registry.json) to the error codes the operation MAY emit. Derived from prose error policy in zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.3 and from error-code-registry.json scope/description. Receivers of an operation SHOULD treat any error code listed here as a known reply shape; codes that map only to the universal failure surface (e.g. internal_error, service_unavailable) are not repeated per operation. cross-link target for zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.3.

rules.universal_codes: Every protected operation MAY additionally return any of: unauthenticated, auth_expired, soft_logged_out, account_locked, account_suspended, account_deactivated, account_erased, did_proof_required, invalid_signature, capability_denied, schema_violation, bad_json, bad_query, missing_param, invalid_param, rate_limited, too_large, conflict, internal_error, service_unavailable, temporarily_unavailable, not_implemented, unsupported_feature, unsupported_event_kind. These are the universal failure surface and are NOT repeated in each operation entry.
rules.operation_specific: operation_specific[] lists the error codes that are semantically tied to this operation's domain logic (event ingest, key claim, blob upload, push gateway, directory ingest, ...). An entry may name either a top-level code from error-code-registry.json `codes` or a sub-code from its `reason_codes` section (carried under a top-level code such as failed_precondition or schema_violation). Consumers discriminate by first matching the entry against the registry's top-level `codes` set; an entry not found there is a reason_code and matches the error reply's `reason_code` field rather than its top-level `code`. Receivers SHOULD recognize and surface these codes specifically.
rules.endpoint_aliases: Each operation entry lists its canonical HTTP method+path alias for human navigation; alternative bindings (gRPC, MQ) inherit the same error code set.
rules.operation_coverage: Every operation_id in artifacts/registry/operation-registry.json MUST appear exactly once in operations[]. An empty operation_specific[] means the operation has no domain-specific reply shape beyond the universal failure surface.

Failure, unauthorized, not-visible, revoked / expired / ambiguous, missing controller, or hidden agent all collapse into a single not_found surface indistinguishable from nonexistence (zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md §9); the op never returns selector candidates.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). Read-only validation: returns active/status/grant-metadata in a 200 body (including not_found / audience_mismatch as statuses, not error replies), so it has no operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface (e.g. bad_json for a malformed id, the universal auth codes when the introspection bearer is missing).

Authenticated S2S issuance. Unknown principal, missing current service binding, wrong source service and unauthorized caller use the universal non-enumerating not_found surface; duplicate_conflict covers request_id reuse with a different canonical intent.

Reserves the complete DID inception operation and issues a durable single-use challenge. proof_invalid covers handoff/DPoP holder mismatch; failed_precondition covers stale or non-holder lease/fence and an operation that does not derive the claimed principal; duplicate_conflict covers request_id reuse or an attempt to replace an existing reserved operation with different bytes.

Resolves an already-published DID and issues a durable single-use control challenge. proof_invalid covers handoff/DPoP holder mismatch; failed_precondition covers rate limiting and DID state that cannot be resolved at the required freshness tier; duplicate_conflict covers the same request_id with different canonical intent; did_not_found and unsupported_did_method cover resolution outcomes that MUST fail closed rather than fall back to caller-supplied history.

Issues the durable single-use challenge that makes abandoning a provisional identity explicit. proof_invalid covers handoff/DPoP holder mismatch; failed_precondition covers a principal_id or did_version_id that is not the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint; identity_creation_lease_fenced covers a stale or non-holder lease/fence; duplicate_conflict covers the same request_id with different canonical intent; identity_creation_already_accepted covers a PCR that is already accepted, for which no abandonment challenge may be issued.

Consumes the abandonment challenge and performs the abandonment in one transaction. proof_invalid covers handoff/DPoP holder mismatch and a handoff replayed from the challenge-issuing call; failed_precondition covers an unknown challenge, a challenge bound to another account, holder, lease or principal, and a confirmation that pins a different principal_id or did_version_id; the two identity_creation_challenge_* codes keep expiry and prior consumption distinct, while an exact replay of the same request_id returns the recorded outcome instead of an error; identity_creation_already_accepted is the stable terminal for a PCR accepted after the challenge was issued and never abandons anything.

Account Authority issuer-ledger session grant issuance. `principal_unknown` is returned when the required principal_id has no verified account binding; the authority must not derive or mint a DID as a fallback. Exact replay returns the byte-identical recorded live outcome after current holder/DPoP/target/digest revalidation; conflicting canonical intent is duplicate_conflict. A recorded expired outcome returns session_grant_replay_expired; revoked/superseded returns session_grant_replay_terminal; an evicted replay record returns session_grant_replay_indeterminate. None may issue a replacement under the same request identity. Proof-kind-specific validation failures remain proof_invalid or the registered Agent lifecycle/authority codes.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): the only client-visible logout entry. It validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain, and completes or durably schedules Principal-side local account/device session cleanup plus to-device/push removal. Does not write ak.account.status, emit ak.device.revoke, or erase durable device authorization. Idempotent — no domain-specific failure beyond the universal surface.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): a validated client-visible account /logout is represented by service-to-service authentication, and the Auth Server logs out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the supplied grant so the rotation chain cannot be resumed. Idempotent: re-presenting an already-logged-out, revoked, unknown, or pruned auth session/grant succeeds with the chain treated as terminated. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they retry ak.gate.account.command.logout.

Native personal agent runtime key pairing. Pairing commit first requires a current controller-owned managed-PCR recovery backup; pending/stale/missing coverage returns agent_pcr_recovery_not_ready without consuming the handle or changing any key/grant. Pairing into an already-deactivated agent principal is terminal. Runtime replacement uses one controller-signed ak.agent.key.authorize with an exact supersedes[] set to atomically replace every prior active authorization dot and record reason=superseded_by_repairing; the service does not synthesize ak.agent.key.revoke Events.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Consumes the Bound AccountHandoff only after the transaction, terminal receipt and coordinator attestation match the current accepted replacement-device projection, then creates one DPoP-bound Standard grant. No temporary recovery grant exists.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger rotation keyed by predecessor_grant_id plus refresh_request_digest. Exact replay returns the recorded successor after current proof revalidation; a conflicting request is duplicate_conflict. One transaction creates the successor and supersedes the predecessor. A recorded successor that is expired or terminal returns the corresponding session_grant_replay_* code and never causes a second successor. The audience remains locked; logged-out or invalid holder/fresh-proof paths retain their existing errors.

Account registration validates the frozen DID operation, root control transcript, exact PCR genesis unit and InitialSessionGrantRequest; relays the unit to the Principal Server; verifies the pcr_genesis_unit receipt; commits the one-account/one-principal binding; then issues the first Standard grant from the durable issuer ledger.

Session grant/access-token revocation. Empty body revokes the current request's session grant; cross grant/device/all_sessions selectors require fresh proof and never revoke device authorization or write durable ak.account.status. The issuer durably records the exact mutation outcome; exact request replay returns that outcome, while the same request identity with different canonical intent returns duplicate_conflict. If replay retention no longer proves whether the mutation committed, session_grant_replay_indeterminate fails closed with zero new state changes.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

OIDC code exchange for a DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant. proof_invalid covers issuer/discovery/state/nonce/redirect_uri/PKCE/body-holder/DPoP binding failures; duplicate_conflict covers reuse of request_id with different canonical request bytes. A live lease owned by another holder is a typed identity_creation_busy outcome, not an error reply.

No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. The live DPoP-bound handoff selects the account and holder; the response is a read-only projection of durable lease or binding state.

Unknown, unauthorized and hidden receipt identifiers are deliberately indistinguishable as not_found.

mls_generation_proposal_fanout_exceeded (409) is the federated counterpart of the self branch: a Direct Conversation activation candidate arriving from the peer service is refused once sixteen not-yet-active candidates already sit under the same predecessor. It is a hard structural cap rather than a rate limit, so the sender MUST NOT treat it as retry-after backoff and MUST NOT quarantine the pair; only the offending candidate is refused, with zero writes.

Exact missing and undisclosable selectors are represented in the successful typed missing sets, not as not_found. limit_exceeded is returned when complete selector accounting cannot fit the negotiated response budget.

The destination KeyPackage authority exposes all target-, device-, inventory-, consent-, capability-, policy-, freshness-, and abuse-related business failures as claim_failed. duplicate_conflict covers claim_request_id reuse with another digest; failed_precondition is limited to a non-secret protocol-state violation that cannot reveal target inventory.

Read-only uncertain-outcome recovery. claim_failed is the opaque stored terminal failure; duplicate_conflict covers a known claim_request_id queried with a different request digest without returning target details.

dependency_missing covers an accepted genesis whose referenced object bytes are not currently available; digest_mismatch and state_mismatch reject ref/raw-byte or RFC 9420 GroupInfo/tree inconsistency; the operation never returns partial material.
Atomically accepts the exact root-committed PCR genesis pair. Transport service authentication is not content authority; any proof, commitment, create-once or fence failure performs zero writes.

Accepts one exact target-signed route artifact into a durable service-local mirror ledger. Authorization/invisibility failures remain minimally disclosing; same durable key with different bytes is duplicate_conflict and performs zero overwrite.

Returns only bounded continuous target-signed material to an already authorized Realm peer. Pre-gate failures use the same minimally disclosing capability_denied response; after the gate, unknown, invisible, not-held, cancelled, expired, gap and fork conditions use the same not_found response. Detailed route reasons are private audit state only and never appear as operation-specific wire codes. Universal rate and size limits remain available.

Optional encrypted-only single-hop Signal peer relay. Only outer peer authentication, trust-domain/destination-endpoint checks, cross-Realm batches and malformed/oversized requests use the universal minimally disclosing failure surface. Per-item unknown Realm/scope/sender, producer-proof, current member delivery-binding, TTL, action-gate, visibility, duplication and recipient failures are silently dropped behind the opaque accepted=true request outcome.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Establishes the local binding after verifying a method-native control or governance-quorum proof against a consumed challenge and a pinned resolved version. Every failure mode is a distinct registered code so a caller can tell a stale challenge from a bad proof from an insufficient quorum without parsing prose.
Issues a single-use control challenge for a resolvable external Organization DID. An unresolvable DID fails closed rather than yielding a challenge no proof could ever satisfy.
Re-proves control at a newer resolved version. A revoked binding is terminal and MUST NOT be revived by refresh; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure.
Withdraws the local binding only. Revoking an already-revoked binding is idempotent and returns the existing terminal receipt rather than an error.

Callers without authority over a binding receive the same did_not_found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the read surface cannot be used to enumerate a deployment's organization relationships.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Publishing or rotating a recovery policy requires authenticated principal isolation, valid Event/lease and signed_fields/signature authority, a known proof-kind enum, and strictly monotonic version/supersedes linkage. frontier_unavailable is the retry-safe response while the submitted Event is valid but its covering control Seal/SealBasis has not materialized.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. A missing accepted policy is a successful response with active_policy=null.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
The Provider verifies a client-signed WebVH inception and returns the stable mapping for the canonical registration key. Conflicting control roots or hosted-document declarations fail closed.

Profile self-service accepts exactly one holder-signed ak.profile.create or ak.profile.update EventInitialSubmission. failed_precondition covers create against an existing Profile, update without an accepted Profile, target/PCR/session authority mismatch, expected_state_digest mismatch, and deterministic profile reducer guards. frontier_unavailable is retry-safe while the valid Control Move lacks accepted Seal coverage. Replaying the same Event identity with different bytes returns duplicate_conflict; exact replay after coverage returns the stored outcome without another aggregate delta. Update patch paths remain limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; avatar_url is rejected.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Holder-bound account self-read. If signed handle-claim evidence or profile/device source refs cannot be verified, the service MUST fail or omit the unverifiable evidence according to disclosure policy; it MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
cas_conflict when expected_revision does not equal the accepted per-key revision; the tombstone is not stored and error.details use account_data_cas_conflict_details.
not_found carries account_data_cas_conflict_details so a caller reading an unset or tombstoned key still learns current_revision for its next compare-and-set write.
cas_conflict when expected_revision does not equal the accepted per-key revision; error.details use account_data_cas_conflict_details so the client can merge and re-issue exactly one write.

Consumes the abandonment challenge and releases the slug and realm-id claims in one transaction. failed_precondition covers an unknown challenge, a challenge bound to another controller, agent, allocation or realm id, credentials replayed from the challenge-issuing call, and a confirmation that pins different values; duplicate_conflict covers the same request_id with different canonical intent; the two agent_provisioning_challenge_* codes keep expiry and prior consumption distinct, while an exact replay of the same request_id returns the recorded outcome instead of an error; agent_pcr_genesis_already_accepted is the stable terminal for a genesis accepted after the challenge was issued and never abandons anything.

agent_deactivated is returned for idempotent re-deactivation of an already-terminal Agent. Missing or invalid proof on the sole controller-authored lifecycle Event returns controller_signed_event_required. Once that Event is accepted, the terminal parent lifecycle gate immediately makes every child authorization ineffective; client-supplied key/grant revoke bundles are schema-invalid and asynchronous cleanup failure cannot roll back deactivation.

Issues the durable single-use challenge that makes abandoning an accepted-but-never-genesised Agent provisioning explicit. failed_precondition covers an agent_id, principal_control_realm_id or allocation_handle that is not the authenticated controller's accepted provisioning; duplicate_conflict covers the same request_id with different canonical intent; agent_pcr_genesis_already_accepted covers a managed Agent PCR genesis that is already accepted, for which no abandonment challenge may be issued.
agent_paused is returned for idempotent re-pause; agent_deactivated is terminal. A lifecycle Event without its required controller proof returns controller_signed_event_required.

Provision a native personal Agent principal. The controller first publishes a PCR-independent managed Agent DID inception. prepare verifies its caller-supplied full_id and returns the exact accepted initial_resolution plus an allocation without generating a DID/private key or choosing a PCR id. commit accepts exactly one controller-signed ak.agent.provision Event that forward-declares the realm id derived from the locally frozen genesis create, atomically projects provision/accountability/selector/realm-id-claim and returns awaiting_pcr_genesis. Separate PCR acceptance advances to awaiting_did_binding; only the controller-signed continuous DID entry 1 with the exact create-locked binding advances to complete and exposes pairing/list/get. requested_scope is a ceiling, not a grant; the service never generates Agent DID/PCR/MLS private state.

Re-open bootstrap pairing or replace an Agent runtime. A renewed pairing MUST issue a fresh single-use `pairing_request_id` + `pairing_code` and MUST leave every previously issued handle permanently unresolvable. An Agent without an active accepted runtime-key authorization uses bootstrap; an Agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle `active` or `paused`) uses replacement, whose single controller-signed authorize Event atomically supersedes prior authorization dots while preserving lifecycle intent. Generic views expose pairing_mode/open-handle fields and readiness blockers, never runtime_state. `deactivated` returns `agent_deactivated`. Neither branch creates, revokes, or re-issues Realm grants; handle expiry has no side effects beyond clearing open-handle fields and recomputing readiness.

Resume revalidates controller, agent key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability grant freshness; any stale precondition fails closed. Sidecar desired membership is re-derived after admission and is not a request precondition. A lifecycle Event without its required controller proof returns controller_signed_event_required.

Accepts a complete controller-authored ak.capability.grant EventInitialSubmission for the agent. The Event envelope proof is the sole durable issuer signature; the CapabilityGrantBody has no inner proof, and the service cannot synthesize or sign the Event. capability_denied surfaces controller-side delegation refusal; agent_paused / agent_deactivated guard the lifecycle gate. An action/resource outside the immutable provision ceiling, or removal/relaxation of a mandatory provision constraint, returns failed_precondition with reason=`agent_grant_exceeds_requested_scope`.
not_found is returned for nonexistent grant_id and for grants not attached to this agent (uniform failure surface).
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.
expected_version must equal the Account Authority's current version for the exact agent/scope slot. First write uses zero; a mismatch returns cas_conflict and performs no write.
not_found is returned both for nonexistent agent principals and for agents not visible to the caller (uniform failure surface, matches ak.self.events.resource.get pattern).

Idempotent ensure: the protocol identity key is `(realm_id, controller_id)` for the Agent Sidecar; `(sidecar_id, normalized_source_context_ref)` deduplicates context mappings without creating another protocol object. `agent_id` is not part of either key. Clients MUST NOT supply Idempotency-Key. sidecar_create_denied is a deliberately generic existence-privacy precondition.
Returns only authenticated-controller-owned Sidecars; another controller's objects do not appear as locked stubs or distinguishable omissions.
Nonexistent, foreign-controller, and unauthorized Sidecar identifiers return the same not_found envelope and timing bucket.
Applet install commit recomputes the InstallPlan, binds approval to plan_digest, persists fan-out idempotency state, and emits registration/grant/profile/membership facts.
Applet revoke validates caller-signed revoke/member submissions against a fresh plan, then resumes a durable event/external/local saga; the first accepted revoke fences future writes.

Ghost Actor provisioning atomically accepts (or idempotently re-confirms) the caller-signed ak.profile.create and ak.identity.accountability_grant Event pair. The server never signs for the Applet service or Ghost. It fails closed on invalid proofs/frontiers, a caller service DID that does not match the active applet registration, a realm outside effective scope (applet_registration_unauthorized), or a ghost_actor_id outside the registered actor namespace (applet_namespace_mismatch). See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §9.1.
Applet install preview validates controller proof, package schema, DID/key binding, namespace conflicts, requested capability actions, and Realm/Circle policy before returning an InstallPlan.
Applet revoke preview recomputes the exact current active-grant, managed-membership, widget-token, and delegated-session plan without side effects.
Publication lease issuance performs the same read-only Event admission as submit. It can reject stale or unknown bases and conflicting idempotency replays, but it never commits an Event.

Only the request target may sign the proposal-terminal rejection. Glare, late reverse requests, slot conflicts and consumed refs fail closed; no Private Consent is written.

Two-phase holder-local Contact request acceptance stores one signed fact and its source receipt. Target resolution and delivery occur later through the receipted peer carrier, so an unresolved target does not reject prepare. It writes no Private Consent and conflicts on byte drift, slot reuse or an already-consumed request ref; frontier_unavailable is retry-safe while the holder PCR actor or accepted Seal frontier is unavailable.
Only the request target may sign a normal acceptance. Glare, late reverse requests, slot conflicts and consumed refs fail closed; rejection uses the separate reject operation.
Issuer-local version/predecessor conflicts quarantine; stale current proof cannot authorize an update or subsequent Contact-based create/send.
A holder-signed tombstone ends one issuer-local Contact generation and cannot be replayed as a scope replacement or Private Consent revocation.
Holder Contact projection from the two holder-signed directional Contact lineages; Consent is never an authority source.
A current Control authority issues one immutable authority Ack after independently validating the proposal and authority basis.

No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface. Unknown / expired / cross-bound ack tokens map to invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) and MUST NOT delete any queued message.
Reusing the same sender-scoped DeviceMessageEnvelope.message_id with different canonical target content returns duplicate_conflict (reason message_id_conflict) and enqueues neither variant.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Idempotent resolver for a pair's one stable conversation. Existing conversations return found or suspended without a KeyPackage lookup. All undisclosable no-binding, peer and directional Contact failures collapse to direct_conversation_unavailable; Consent is not queried. Typed success states are found, creation_required, suspended and temporarily_unavailable.

Requester-scoped durable repair outbox. Missing or undisclosable pair authority collapses to direct_conversation_unavailable; stale rejoin/generation/evidence is failed_precondition; reuse of request_id with a different canonical request is duplicate_conflict. No recipient device or Agent-runtime target is disclosed.

Service-authenticated atomic recipient enqueue. Reuse of (Source-Service-ID, request_id) with a changed request digest is duplicate_conflict and writes nothing. Invalid/stale portable requester authority or repair gates are failed_precondition; hidden pair/recipient state is direct_conversation_unavailable. Partial human-device fanout and Agent endpoint fallback are forbidden.
A request_id intent conflict, create-if-absent or renewal CAS mismatch, or an unaccepted/stale principal authority writes no binding draft beyond an exact replay of the original durable challenge.

Challenge reuse with different material, expiry, current-binding CAS loss, proof failure or stale authority consumes and installs nothing. Exact replay of a committed request returns the stored byte-identical binding outcome.

Event submission. Per-event rejections appear in response.rejected[] with one of these codes. ak.invite.claim-specific reducer reasons remain internal/audit-facing when exposed through non-enumerable invite claim flows. mls_generation_proposal_fanout_exceeded (409) refuses the seventeenth not-yet-active Direct Conversation activation candidate under one predecessor; it is a hard structural cap and not a rate limit, so it carries no retry window, it is never rate_limited (429), and it refuses only that candidate with zero writes while leaving the pair unquarantined.

Client-signed Seal submission. The receiver recomputes coverage, completeness and state roots; verifies signer authority against the predecessor notary cell; rejects stale generation, partial bootstrap coverage or frontier races; and holds future-skewed Seals for retry instead of permanently rejecting them.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

not_found preserves Realm/scope visibility; mls_governance_anchor_unreachable means no verified path exists from the exact caller-trusted anchor and permits retry only with another locally trusted anchor/service; mls_governance_proof_bounds_exceeded means the complete logical bundle exceeds a v1 count/byte/chunk bound and forbids partial output; frontier_unavailable covers temporarily missing accepted Seal material or an unavailable expected_bundle_digest and permits restarting at chunk 0; state_mismatch covers incomplete covered/control materialization; signature_invalid covers an unverifiable Seal/Event/chunk commitment; profile_unsupported rejects unsupported binding or reducer profiles.
not_found is returned both for nonexistent events and for events hidden by visibility (uniform failure surface).
Issue fails closed when the authenticated principal reaches the active-locator limit or the requested TTL violates deployment policy.
Repeated revocation by the same principal is idempotent; unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.
Unknown, consumed, revoked, or cross-principal locator ids are not enumerable and return not_found.
